description: Named rotational camera-shake presets used by unguarded player-side battle damage; each row supplies legacy ULegacyCameraShake duration, blend and pitch/yaw oscillator values.

ID.simple: Camera shake preset name, e.g. NormalBlow_N.
ID.technical: Exported as ID but declared in C++ as FName Id (the export's ImportKeyField is Id). The runtime playback lookup does not read the struct member: FStudioBattleSystem2E0::PlayCameraShakes takes each FName from a Damage row's Id_CameraShake_Attacker or Id_CameraShake_Receiver array, skips NAME_None (exported as "None"), scans DataTables->CameraShakeDataTables (+0x7B0) in order, and accepts the first UDataTable::FindRow<FGameDataTableRow_CameraShake> hit with warnings disabled. A missing ID yields a null row and no shake. The master export has 48 unique named rows; every row key equals its ID, and all 10 by-character CameraShake exports are exact subsets of those rows.

OscillationDuration.technical: float copied verbatim to UGameCameraShake::OscillationDuration by the AddCameraShake initializer. In UE 5.1 ULegacyCameraShake, a positive value is a finite duration, zero disables oscillation, and a negative value is indefinite; all exported values are positive and range from 0.2 s (basic rows) to 2.0 s (CP_140 rows). The reconstructed row constructor defaults it to 0.0; exported rows always supply their own value.

OscillationBlendInTime.simple: Fade-in time at the start of the shake.
OscillationBlendInTime.technical: float seconds copied verbatim to UGameCameraShake::OscillationBlendInTime. UE 5.1 scales the oscillation from 0 to 1 over this interval. The row constructor default is 0.0; exported values range from 0.0 (three CP_040_ATTACKH_02_01_* rows) to 0.2 s (CP_010_ATTACKE_01_01_3), with 0.05 s most common.

OscillationBlendOutTime.simple: Fade-out time at the end of the shake.
OscillationBlendOutTime.technical: float seconds copied verbatim to UGameCameraShake::OscillationBlendOutTime. UE 5.1 starts fading from 1 to 0 when remaining oscillation time falls below this value, so a blend-out equal to or longer than the duration fades from the start. The row constructor default is 0.0; exported values range from 0.05 s to 2.0 s, with 0.05 s for TEST/MultiHit/shot rows and longer tails for cursed and CP_140 rows.

RotOscillation_Pitch_Amplitude.technical: float copied verbatim to GameShake->RotOscillation.Pitch.Amplitude. The engine adds the oscillator result to a FRotator pitch, so this is a degree offset; 0 disables visible pitch oscillation. Exported values range from 0.0 to 10.0. The V-suffixed NormalStumble/NormalBlow rows and CP_070_ATTACKG_01_01_* rows use 0 with nonzero yaw amplitude; the row constructor default is also 0.0.

RotOscillation_Pitch_Frequency.technical: float copied verbatim to GameShake->RotOscillation.Pitch.Frequency. In the checked UE 5.1 FFOscillator implementation, phase advances by DeltaSeconds * Frequency before Sin, so the stored value is angular radians/second, not degrees or hertz (60-100 is about 9.5-15.9 cycles/s). Exported values range from 50.0 to 100.0; a row with zero pitch amplitude shows no pitch effect regardless of this value. The row constructor default is 0.0.

RotOscillation_Yaw_Amplitude.technical: float copied verbatim to GameShake->RotOscillation.Yaw.Amplitude. The engine adds the oscillator result to a FRotator yaw, so this is a degree offset; 0 disables visible yaw oscillation. Exported values range from 0.0 to 10.0. The H-suffixed NormalStumble/NormalBlow rows use 0 with nonzero pitch amplitude, while the row constructor default is also 0.0.

RotOscillation_Yaw_Frequency.technical: float copied verbatim to GameShake->RotOscillation.Yaw.Frequency. As with pitch, UE 5.1 advances phase by DeltaSeconds * Frequency before Sin, so this is angular radians/second, not hertz. Exported values range from 40.0 to 100.0; a row with zero yaw amplitude shows no yaw effect regardless of this value, and the row constructor default is 0.0.

notes: Loading and lookup: AGameDataTableManager registers the single primary-asset loader name CameraShakeDataTable (GameDataTableManager.cpp:426) and resolves that loader into CameraShakeDataTables at +0x7B0 (GameDataTableManager.cpp:253; declaration at GameDataTableManager.h:164). PlayCameraShakes scans that array in order and the first table containing the row wins; FindRow is called with bWarnIfRowMissing=false (GameBattleDamage.cpp:233-240).

Damage-side conditions: In ApplyCharacterDamage the guarded branch returns without any shake (GameBattleDamage.cpp:502-607). Only the unguarded branch plays shakes: if the attacker is a player it uses Id_CameraShake_Attacker and also starts the hit marker/force feedback; otherwise, in an else-if, if the receiver is a player it uses Id_CameraShake_Receiver (GameBattleDamage.cpp:609-622). The attacker test therefore has precedence. ApplyShikigamiDamage uses Id_CameraShake_Attacker only, and only when the attacker is a player (GameBattleDamage.cpp:870-873).

Index and sentinel behavior: Every exported Damage shake-ID array has exactly two FName slots, and the exported sentinel for NAME_None is the string "None", which PlayCameraShakes skips. Index 0 selects UGameCameraShake_01 and index 1 selects UGameCameraShake_02; only CP_081 damage rows populate slot 1, with CP_081_ATTACK_01. PlayCameraShake indexes a two-element raw C++ array without a bounds check, so a longer or differently indexed Damage array would be invalid even though no export does that. Scale is hard-coded to 1.0 at every call site.

Playback gates and lifecycle: AGameCameraManager::PlayCameraShake returns null when the row is null, the inherited cached UCameraModifier_CameraShake is null, Scale <= 0, or ACameraManager::bCameraShakeEnabled is false (GameCameraManager.cpp:251-254). That flag defaults to true (Framework/Public/CameraManager.h:20 and GameSettings.h:23) and is written by AGameManager::SetCameraShakeEnabled (GameManagerGraphics.cpp:218-221). Battle finish/KO/time-up paths can later call StopAllCameraShakes(true) (GameBattleState_05.cpp:203; GameBattleState_10.cpp:502, 595, 614, 640).

Row scope: The row struct has only FName Id plus the seven float fields checked here. The initializer writes only duration, blend times and pitch/yaw oscillator amplitude/frequency; it writes no roll, location or FOV oscillator and no camera-anim/asset reference. The selected UGameCameraShake, UGameCameraShake_01 and UGameCameraShake_02 subclasses add no members in the reconstruction (GameCameraShake*.h). All seven float fields default to 0.0 in the reconstructed row constructor (0x32d47f0), although ULegacyCameraShake's own CDO has nonzero blend defaults that are overwritten here.

Export coverage: The master datatables/CameraShakeDataTable.json has 48 unique rows; 10 datatables_by_character/*/CameraShakeDataTable.json shards contain exact subsets with no changed values. Across all 60 exported Damage files, every referenced shake ID exists in the master export; 37 camera-shake IDs are referenced by a Damage shake-ID array and 11 IDs are not referenced by any such array (mostly character-specific rows; CursedBlow_H is one exception). TEST is referenced by CN_041 damage rows, so it is not merely an unused test row.

Evidence strength: The runtime description above is reconstructed C++ backed by static retail RVAs, not retail Blueprint graphs. status/functions.json records 0x105d9a0 (PlayCameraShake) as byte-matched and 0x32d47f0 (row constructor) as an ICF-matched leaf, while 0x102b3a0 (PlayCameraShakes) is BEHAV-certified but not byte-matched (Tools/verify/BEHAV/records/RD05.json). No Blueprint-derived behavior is claimed. A separate GameDebugManager::CameraShakeDisabled flag exists and defaults false, but no reader for it was found in the available source, so it is not treated as a traced playback gate.

usages.detail: Registers CameraShakeDataTable as a primary asset to load; line 253 resolves it into CameraShakeDataTables at +0x7B0.
PlayCameraShakes resolves non-None Damage IDs to rows over +0x7B0, first match wins, then calls the player camera manager with the array index and scale 1.0.
Unguarded character damage selects the attacker array when the attacker is a player, otherwise the receiver array when the receiver is a player; guarded hits return earlier.
Shikigami damage plays only the attacker shake array and only for a player attacker.
PlayCameraShake gates on row/modifier/scale/bCameraShakeEnabled, copies all seven numeric fields in an initializer, and selects _01 for index 0 or _02 for index 1.
The saved game setting can disable camera shake by writing AGameCameraManager::bCameraShakeEnabled; the default is true.
